findings.title: Sharded path interpolates the same targets at least three times
findings.body: `runShardSplitQuery` now calls `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, scopedVars, filters)` on every target. Each shard sub-request is then passed to `runSplitQuery`, which this PR also changed to call `applyTemplateVariables` on every target. `DataSourceWithBackend.query`, reached through `datasource.runQuery`, applies it a third time. Ad hoc filters (`request.filters`) are now added to the expression at every layer, so the stream selector can pick up the same label filter several times. Already-substituted variable values are also re-scanned, so a value containing `$name` or `${name}` text can be expanded a second time. The updated shard test even asserts `applyTemplateVariables` is called 5 times for one query (1 + 4 sub-requests). Interpolate once at the top, or give the inner `runSplitQuery` a way to skip interpolation when it is called from the shard splitter.

findings.title: Interpolated targets are still re-interpolated downstream, and filters are applied pre-split and again later
findings.body: `runSplitQuery` now applies `applyTemplateVariables` with `request.scopedVars` and `request.filters` to the targets before building the sub-requests. Those interpolated targets are then sent to `datasource.runQuery`, which goes through `DataSourceWithBackend.query` and interpolates them again, adding ad hoc filters a second time. The change is needed so that `isLogsQuery`, `calculateStep` and `querySupportsSplitting` see resolved text. The non-idempotent steps (ad hoc filter injection, regex escaping of multi-value variables) now run on already-processed expressions. Nothing in the PR checks that a second pass is a no-op, for example with several ad hoc filters or a multi-value variable inside a regex matcher.

findings.title: Brittle call-count assertion locks in redundant interpolation; duplicate test name
findings.body: `expect(datasource.applyTemplateVariables).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)` depends on 1 initial interpolation plus 4 sub-requests, each re-interpolating inside `runSplitQuery`. The assertion breaks whenever the shard count changes, and it enshrines the double interpolation as expected behaviour. It does not show that interpolation happens before execution, which is what the test title claims. This test is also named 'Interpolates queries before running', almost identical to the new 'Interpolates queries before execution' test a few lines above, which makes the two hard to tell apart. The new test only checks the first `runQuery` call and does not check ad hoc filters passed via `request.filters`, the main new input to `applyTemplateVariables`.
